design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 of auto_loan_servicing (category finance), env_0041_online_used_car_retailer.

[Step 0 - draw] `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0041_online_used_car_retailer/tasks/auto_loan_servicing --task 1` printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0041_online_used_car_retailer/auto_loan_servicing/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}. Assignment: goodwill credit (root) 6, cure payment 4.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: finance_ext_returned_payment_fee, finance_ext_late_fee_assessment, finance_ext_deferral_qualifying_payment, finance_ext_deferral_fee and their four tools (fee assessments, the partial payment, the deferral). Claimed here: finance_ext_cure_payment (pay_past_due_installment_fb9b9167, owner=user, a scheduled-installment payment that moves the due date - distinct from task 0's partial payment, which never moves it) and finance_ext_goodwill_late_fee_credit (credit_goodwill_late_fee_132adaff, a principal credit). After this task every extended policy is covered and nothing is left idle.

[Why a good test] Calvin asks one thing: take the September late fee off. The goodwill rule says relief is not fixed until a scheduled-installment payment has posted for the installment the fee was charged on; the ledger shows the 2026-09-01 installment unpaid (next due 2026-09-01, last scheduled payment 2026-08-01). So the agent must hand the customer his own cure payment, computing its amount (4 factors) and its waterfall split, and only then compute the goodwill credit (6 factors) on the world that payment produces - including the cure-speed factor that the payment itself moves.

[Design thesis] surface goal "take the late fee off" -> goodwill credit (root) waits on a scheduled payment for the late installment -> cure payment -> terminal: payment entry + fee-paid entry, principal credit 7.75 naming the fee, next due 2026-10-01, fees due 0.00, principal 23295.23. Breadth: purchase program (Kestrel Inspected) and vehicle count (2 vehicle-price charges), KestrelCare Silver (warranty) and GAP Standard (gap), 12- and 24-month windows of late fees, waivers and returns, tenure count, contract age, days past due.

[Problem-tree card] Root finance_ext_goodwill_late_fee_credit (agent). Edge G -> U: kind value_input, gate cure_days, form state, sentence "Goodwill relief on a late fee is not fixed until a scheduled-installment payment has posted on the contract for the installment that late fee was charged on." (negated direction: the desk says relief is not given until the installment is paid). Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until'; waited side is a ledger entry kind (scheduled-installment payment) for a named installment; no tool, id or snake_case token; scope exactly the installment the late fee names. Exactly one write of this difficulty posts a scheduled-installment payment: pay_past_due_installment_fb9b9167 (task 0's partial payment is a different entry kind). Opening evidence: late fee 2026-09-12 names 2026-09-01; latest scheduled payment is for 2026-08-01; next due date 2026-09-01. Deletion sensitivity: without the payment the credit computes 9.25 instead of 7.75. user_scenario names no prerequisite; the tools validate none. At least one write (the cure payment) is the customer's own, unlocked and handed over by the agent.

[Base-invariant card] Cure payment (finance_payment_posted): finance_payment_application.payment_active (status active), card_limits (online bank transfer, not a debit card). Goodwill credit (finance_principal_credited): finance_principal_credits.credit_state (status active). Goodwill allowance (overwritten base sentence, now counting waivers and credits): reliefs fewer than 12 whole months back = 0 (the 2025-06-12 waiver is 15 months back) < tier B allowance 1, so relief is allowed. No time gate applies.

[Business-object card] Contract fc (only one). Late fee relieved = 829a5966 (2026-09-12, 15.00, installment 2026-09-01). Excluded: 2026-03-12 late fee (paid 2026-03-14, older) and 2025-06-12 late fee (waived as goodwill the same day). Cure object = installment 2026-09-01; 2026-10-01 is in grace on 2026-10-06 and is not brought current.

[Factor card] Cure payment (4): tenure catch-up 5 days (multi-source: 35 days past due AND 24 paid; baseline 662.51); program 4 days (purchase Kestrel Inspected; baseline 666.59); contract-age x0.5 (26 months; baseline 719.54); lateness deposit 10.00 (2 late fees in 12 months; baseline 672.88). Whole baseline 636.22 vs 682.88. Goodwill credit (6): share 0.5 (multi-source: 2 late fees AND no return; baseline 13.75); cure speed x0.8 (24 days, moved by the cure payment; baseline 9.25); prior relief -1.50 (2025-06-12 waiver inside 24 months; baseline 9.25); protection +2.00 (warranty Silver financed + GAP active; baseline 5.75); tenure +0.75 (25 paid after the payment; baseline 7.00); repeat buyer +0.50 (2 vehicle-price charges; baseline 7.25). Whole baseline 15.00 vs 7.75. Near-misses: the 2025-06-12 late fee is outside the 12-month windows but inside 24; the 2026-10-01 installment is past due but within grace.

[initial_state rows] customers; purchase_orders (2: cash 2021 Honda Accord LX under Kestrel Value Line, financed 2019 Ford F-150 XLT under Kestrel Inspected); purchase_transactions (2 vehicle-price charges); finance_contracts (tier B, 621.22, 12.69%, principal 23433.16, fees 15.00, next due 2026-09-01); finance_transactions (30: funding, 24 payments, 3 late fees, a goodwill waiver, 1 fee-paid entry; each consistent with the extended late-fee policy on its date); service_contracts (Silver active financed); gap_waivers (Standard active on fc). The historical fees 17.08, 15.53 and 15.00 are what the late-fee policy gives on 2025-06-12, 2026-03-12 and 2026-09-12 for a Georgia registration.

[Persona] Calvin is gruff and brief; volunteers the late fee notice, that the September payment slipped, and that this is his second Kestrel vehicle (true: two purchase orders). Identity (9125553108, 3540, 31405) on request, email/vehicle if asked. Passive: pays the September payment himself exactly as handed, only if told it must be paid first; grumbles once but accepts partial relief; ends when told the relief is on the loan.

[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify (phone, SSN4, ZIP) -> find_finance_contracts -> find_finance_transactions -> find_purchase_orders -> find_purchase_transactions -> find_service_contracts -> find_gap_waivers -> unlock_user / customer calls pay_past_due_installment (installment 2026-09-01, next due 2026-10-01, 682.88 = 537.70 + 15.00 + 130.18) -> unlock/call credit_goodwill_late_fee (fee 829a5966, 7.75).

[Verification] The verification run (check_compute.py --task 1) on the handling-time worlds: cure payment 682.88 (baseline 636.22), goodwill credit 7.75 (baseline 15.00), factor baselines as in factor_sensitivity; prerequisite sensitivity: credit without the payment 9.25.

[Blind draft from visible context] From the goodwill rule's prerequisite sentence the reader looks for a scheduled payment for 2026-09-01 and finds none; the cure rule (found as the policy whose write is a scheduled-installment payment) gives 1 installment, 15.00 fees, 4.5 catch-up days and a 10.00 deposit = 682.88 with the 537.70/15.00/130.18 split; the goodwill rule then gives 7.75. Same order and numbers as gold.

[Gates run for this task] From the repository root, with DIFF=env/env_0041_online_used_car_retailer/tasks/auto_loan_servicing: check_extended.py $DIFF --task 1 -> EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools.py $DIFF --task 1 -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks.py $DIFF --task 1 -> REPLAY OK (deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure = initial_state); check_solvability.py $DIFF --task 1 -> SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute.py $DIFF --task 1 -> COMPUTE OK (handling-time recompute = expected = gold, every factor baseline moves the result and equals factor_sensitivity, whole baseline = baseline_result); check_grounding.py $DIFF --task 1 -> GROUNDING OK; check_cache_diff.py $DIFF --task 1 -> CACHE-DIFF INFO (no cache trap designed); check_cross_fire.py $DIFF --task 1 -> SCOPE OK. check_traceability.py is deferred until the KB is published.

[Revisions] r1: the relief is a principal credit (billing correction) rather than a waiver, because the cure payment's waterfall pays the open late fee before principal - waiving a paid fee would be inconsistent; the base goodwill sentence is declared overwritten so credits and waivers count alike.
r2 (audit round 2, audits/policy_task/auto_loan_servicing; task 1 PASS, charter observations closed): O-2/O-3 - the goodwill rule and the credit tool now say 'goodwill relief on a late fee' without the second 'the borrower has paid' wording, so the prerequisite sentence is the only statement of the dependency. O-4 - the allowance and the prior-relief reduction now state exactly what they count ('every waived late fee and every billing-correction principal credit on the contract'); on this world that is the 2025-06-12 waiver only, so the figures are unchanged (0 reliefs in 12 months, 1 in 24 months, credit 7.75). O-6 - the cure policy now declares its overwrite of base finance_payment_application ('A scheduled-installment payment advances the next due date by one month for each full monthly payment it contains, never beyond the maturity date;') and its own sentence keeps 'never beyond the maturity date'; here 682.88 contains one full monthly payment and brings one installment current, so both readings give 2026-10-01. Re-ran every gate on the revised charter (all OK, values unchanged).
user_scenario:
You are Calvin Lindqvist, 46, a crane operator at the port in Savannah, Georgia. You financed a 2019 Ford F-150 through Kestrel two years ago, and it is the second vehicle you have bought from them. A notice in the Kestrel app shows you were charged a late fee in September, because your September truck payment slipped while you were working double shifts. You are plain-spoken and a bit gruff, you do not like small talk, and you feel that a customer who pays like you do deserves a break.

You open by saying you got hit with a late fee on your September truck payment and asking to have that September late fee taken off. You do not know your loan number. When the representative asks who you are, you give your mobile number 9125553108; to confirm your identity you give the last four of your Social Security number, 3540, and your home ZIP code, 31405. Only if they ask for more, your email is calvin.lindqvist.sav@outlook.com. If they ask which vehicle, it is the 2019 Ford F-150.

You let the representative handle the fee for you. If the representative tells you the September payment has to be paid before anything can be done about the fee, you agree to pay it today from your checking account; when they hand you the payment in the Kestrel app, you enter exactly what they give you, the same total, the same split between interest, fees and principal, the same dates and the loan reference they read out, and you read back the confirmation it shows. If they tell you that you will only get part of the fee back, you grumble once that you expected all of it but you accept it. You do not know any amounts yourself and never propose one. Once the representative confirms the late fee relief has been put on your loan, you say thanks and hang up.

edges.condition: The loan history carries a scheduled-installment payment entry whose installment due date is the installment the most recent late-fee entry names, and the contract's next due date has moved past that installment.
edges.policy_source: Goodwill relief on a late fee is not fixed until a scheduled-installment payment has posted on the contract for the installment that late fee was charged on.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The most recent late fee (2026-09-12, 15.00) names installment 2026-09-01, and no scheduled-installment payment for 2026-09-01 exists: the latest one is dated 2026-08-01 for installment 2026-08-01, and the contract's next due date is still 2026-09-01.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 9 posts the scheduled-installment payment for 2026-09-01 dated 2026-10-06: next due date 2026-10-01, cure_days -42 -> 24, cure-speed factor 1 -> 0.8, installments paid 24 -> 25.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite: the cure payment must precede the goodwill credit by the goodwill rule's prerequisite sentence; no parallel edge exists. The credit is computed on the world after the payment (credit 7.75); computed before it, it would be 9.25 and would relieve a fee still unpaid.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the cure payment the goodwill credit computes to 9.25 instead of 7.75 (cure-speed factor 1 instead of 0.8), the payment entry and fee-paid entry are missing, next due date stays 2026-09-01 and fees due stay 15.00.
